senses.title: In spite of what was said
senses.definition: used to say that something is still true or will still happen despite the obstacle just mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示尽管刚提到某种阻碍，某事仍然成立或仍会发生
senses.example: The shop was closed, but we went anyway and waited outside.
senses.exampleCN: 店已经关门了，但我们还是去了，在外面等着。
senses.why: Built from 'any way', the word first allows every route; once no route is ruled out, the obstacle loses its power to stop the action.
senses.whyCN: 由「任何一条路」构成，这个词先允许每条路线；一旦没有路线被排除，阻碍就失去了拦住行动的力量。

senses.title: Besides, as a further point
senses.definition: used to add a supporting point that strengthens what has just been said
senses.definitionCN: 用于补上一个支持性的论点，加强刚说过的话
senses.example: It is too late to call; anyway, she has probably gone to bed.
senses.exampleCN: 现在打电话太晚了；再说，她大概已经睡了。
senses.why: The concessive word can also lean the other way: since the first point stands, a second point is added on top of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个让步词也能往另一边倾：既然第一点已经立住，第二点就叠加上去。

senses.title: To change or close a topic
senses.titleCN: （用于转换或收束话题）总之；好了
senses.definition: used in conversation to move to a new topic or to bring the present one to an end
senses.definitionCN: 用于谈话中转向新话题，或把当前话题收住
senses.example: Anyway, let us not waste the whole afternoon on this.
senses.exampleCN: 总之，我们别把整个下午都耗在这件事上。
senses.why: A word that brushes obstacles aside is equally handy for brushing a conversation aside, so it becomes a hinge in speech.
senses.whyCN: 一个能把阻碍拂开的词，同样方便把一段对话拂开，于是它成了口语里的转轴。

senses.title: In any way one likes
senses.definition: in any manner, especially in the phrase anyway you like
senses.definitionCN: 以任何方式，尤用于短语 anyway you like
senses.example: You can arrange the books anyway you like.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以按自己喜欢的任何方式摆放这些书。
senses.why: This is the oldest literal layer: any plus way, every method still open before habit picks one.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的字面层：any 加 way，在习惯挑定一种之前，每种方法都还敞着。

intro.en: Anyway is a native compound of any and way, and its history runs from a literal 'any road' to a conversational shrug.
intro.cn: anyway 是 any 与 way 的本族复合，它的历史从字面的「任何一条路」一路走到会话中的一耸肩。

items.en: Weg meant 'way, road, path', and ǣnig 'any' was already available to combine with it.
items.cn: weg 表示「路、道路、路径」，而 ǣnig「任何一个」当时已可与它组合。

items.en: The phrase any way is common in the literal sense 'by any road or means'.
items.cn: 短语 any way 常见，取字面义「以任何道路或手段」。

items.en: The two words close into anyway, and the concessive sense 'in spite of that' begins to appear.
items.cn: 两个词合拢为 anyway，让步义「尽管如此」开始出现。

items.en: In everyday speech anyway becomes a topic changer, used to add a point or to end a subject.
items.cn: 在日常口语里，anyway 成为转话题的词，用于补一点或结束一个话题。

items.en: The concessive and conversational senses dominate, while the literal 'any way' survives in phrases such as anyway you like.
items.cn: 让步义与会话义占主导，字面的「任何方式」则活在 anyway you like 这类短语里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the close compounds and variants; the near-meaning group gathers connectives that carry the same concession or addition.
note.cn: 形近组收与它最接近的复合词和变体；近义组收承担同样让步或补充关系的连接词。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in any way or in spite of that, the closest twin.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「以任何方式」或「无论如何」，是 anyway 最接近的孪生词。

entries.definition: A colloquial variant of anyway, frequent in informal speech.
entries.definitionCN: anyway 的口语变体，常见于非正式谈话。

entries.definition: An archaic adverb meaning in any manner.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧副词，义为「以任何方式」。

entries.definition: A connective meaning despite that, used to contrast two statements.
entries.definitionCN: 连接词，义为「然而、尽管如此」，用于对比前后两句。

entries.definition: A formal connective meaning in spite of that.
entries.definitionCN: 正式连接词，义为「尽管如此」，书面语气更强。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning without being affected by the circumstances.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「不加理会、无论如何」，强调不受情况影响。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in addition, used to add a further point.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「此外、况且」，与 anyway 的补充义最接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real any-plus-way structure and the positions the word takes in a sentence.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 any 加 way 结构，以及这个词在句中占据的位置。

normal.en: Split it: any plus way. Every road is open, so no closed door can stop you.
normal.cn: 拆开看：any 加 way，每条路都开着，所以没有一扇关上的门能拦住你。

normal.en: It often sits at the start, then states the point that survives: anyway, we tried.
normal.cn: 它常坐在句首，然后说出仍然成立的那一点：反正我们试过了。

normal.en: Its twin anyhow carries the same shrug; anyways is the casual spoken form.
normal.cn: 孪生词 anyhow 带着同样的耸肩，anyways 则是随意的口语形式。

normal.en: Use it to add a reason: too late, and anyway she has gone to bed.
normal.cn: 用它补一条理由：太晚了，再说她已经睡了。

normal.en: Use it to close a subject, as a hand waves the rest of the talk away.
normal.cn: 用它收住话题，就像一只手把剩下的话挥走。

abstract.en: Picture a road closed by rain, and a walker stepping around the barrier without hesitation.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被雨封住的路，走路的人毫不犹豫地绕过障碍继续走。

abstract.en: The word is momentum turned into sound: the obstacle is noted, then left behind.
abstract.cn: 这个词是惯性变成了声音：记下阻碍，然后把它留在身后。

abstract.en: In talk it works as a door: one topic closes, another opens.
abstract.cn: 在谈话里它像一扇门：一个话题关上，另一个打开。

examples.en: The shop was closed, but we went anyway and waited outside.
examples.cn: 店已经关门了，但我们还是去了，在外面等着。

examples.en: Anyway, let us not waste the whole afternoon on this.
examples.cn: 总之，我们别把整个下午都耗在这件事上。

examples.en: You can arrange the books anyway you like.
examples.cn: 你可以按自己喜欢的任何方式摆放这些书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安妮为」——雨把路封了，安妮还是说「为到现场，怎么走都行」：无论如何

root: anyway 由 any「任何一个」与 way「路、方式」在本族英语中复合而成。中古英语短语 any way 取字面义「以任何道路或手段」；十六世纪合拢为 anyway，并出现让步义「尽管如此」；十九世纪在日常口语中又成为转换或收束话题的词；现代让步义与会话义占主导，字面义保留在 anyway you like 一类短语中。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses fan out from 'any road': the concession that survives an obstacle, the added supporting point, the conversational hinge, and the literal open manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法从「任何一条路」展开：越过阻碍仍然成立的让步、补上的支持论点、会话里的转轴，以及字面意义上的开放方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road blocked by rain, and a walker who steps around it without pausing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被雨封住的路，走路的人不停顿地绕了过去。

branches.en: THE CONCESSION LINE: the obstacle is real, yet the action goes on.
branches.cn: 让步线：阻碍是真的，行动却继续。

branches.en: THE ADDITION LINE: a second reason is stacked on the first.
branches.cn: 补充线：第二条理由叠在第一条之上。

branches.en: THE HINGE LINE: one subject closes and another opens.
branches.cn: 转轴线：一个话题关上，另一个打开。

branches.en: THE LITERAL LINE: any road, any method, still open to choice.
branches.cn: 字面线：任何一条路、任何一种方法，仍向选择敞开。

branches.en: THE SHRUG LINE: the same gesture waves off both obstacles and side topics.
branches.cn: 耸肩线：同一个动作既挥开阻碍，也挥开枝节话题。

intro.en: Anyway is an open compound: any plus way, with a small family of variants on how, wise and -s.
intro.cn: anyway 是透明的复合词：any 加 way，并有一小族以 how、wise、-s 构成的变体。

latinIntro.en: Anyway has no Latin source; Latin via is a semantic parallel for 'way', not an ancestor.
latinIntro.cn: anyway 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语的 via 只是「路」的语义平行词，并非祖先。

items.example: Anyway, the bus came at last.
items.exampleCN: 反正公交车最后还是来了。

items.example: The way to the mill is narrow.
items.exampleCN: 去磨坊的那条路很窄。

items.meaning: in any way; in spite of that
items.example: Anyhow, the key was under the mat.
items.exampleCN: 不管怎样，钥匙就在门垫下面。

items.meaningCN: 口语中的「反正、无论如何」
items.example: Anyways, I will call you tomorrow.
items.exampleCN: 反正我明天会给你打电话。

items.example: He was not anywise prepared for snow.
items.exampleCN: 他对下雪毫无准备。

items.meaningCN: 在任何地方；到任何地方
items.example: We could meet anywhere near the station.
items.exampleCN: 我们可以在车站附近的任何地方见面。

items.example: Someway, the door was forced open.
items.exampleCN: 门不知怎么被强行打开了。

items.example: A stone pathway leads to the gate.
items.exampleCN: 一条石径通向大门。

items.meaning: one or some, no matter which
items.example: Any road out of the valley will do.
items.exampleCN: 出山谷的任何一条路都行。

definition_zh: 任何地方；无论哪里；随便哪儿
definition_en: in or to any place at all, used in questions, negatives, and statements of total range
core_image: 把地图摊开，手指落在哪儿都算数
scene: 旧书店的老板把一张卷边的地图铺在柜台上。We could not find that village anywhere on the map.
sceneCN: 这里 anywhere 是「任何地方」（第 1 个义项：在否定句中表示连一个地方也没有）；句意为「我们在地图上任何地方都找不到那个村子」。画面里有旧书店的柜台、卷边的地图和俯身查找的老板。

pos.zh: 副词：任何地方；无论哪里；随便哪儿

collocations.zh: 别的任何地方；其他地方
随便哪个地方；任何地方

derivatives.zh: 美式口语中与 anywhere 同义的复合词，由 any 与 place 构成
与 anywhere 并列的复合词，由 every 与 where 构成，义为「到处」
与 anywhere 并列的复合词，由 no 与 where 构成，义为「哪里都不」
与 anywhere 并列的复合词，由 some 与 where 构成，义为「某处」

senses.title: Any place, after a negative
senses.definition: used after a negative to mean that no place at all is involved or reached
senses.definitionCN: 用在否定词之后，表示完全不涉及或到达任何地方
senses.example: We could not find that village anywhere on the map.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在地图上任何地方都找不到那个村子。
senses.why: Where opens the whole map and any leaves every point available, so a negative shuts the entire surface at once.
senses.whyCN: where 摊开整张地图，any 又让每个点都可用，于是一个否定一下子把整片表面都关上。

senses.title: Any place, in a question
senses.definition: used in questions to ask whether some place, whichever it is, has been tried or visited
senses.definitionCN: 用于疑问句，询问是否试过或去过某个地方，而不限定是哪里
senses.example: Have you looked anywhere for the missing keys?
senses.exampleCN: 你有没有到任何地方找过那串丢失的钥匙？
senses.why: In a question the speaker does not know which point on the map is relevant, so the whole map is offered at once.
senses.whyCN: 在疑问句里，说话人不知道地图上哪个点才相关，于是把整张地图一次性摊开。

senses.title: Any place at all, for range
senses.titleCN: 任何地方（用于肯定强调）
senses.definition: used in affirmative statements to stress that every place is included without restriction
senses.definitionCN: 用于肯定陈述，强调每一个地方都被无限制地包括在内
senses.example: You can sit anywhere you like in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅里你想坐哪儿都行。
senses.why: In a statement the open map turns into a general permission: no seat and no place is reserved.
senses.whyCN: 在陈述句中，敞开的地图变成普遍许可：没有哪个座位、哪个地方是被预留的。

senses.title: To make any progress
senses.titleCN: 取得任何进展（用于 get anywhere）
senses.definition: in phrases such as get anywhere, to reach any result or make any progress
senses.definitionCN: 用于 get anywhere 一类短语，表示达到任何结果或取得任何进展
senses.example: Without the old records, we will not get anywhere with this case.
senses.exampleCN: 没有那些旧档案，这个案子我们不会有任何进展。
senses.why: Progress is pictured as a journey to a place; if every place is open, then getting anywhere means getting somewhere at all.
senses.whyCN: 进展被画成一段走到某地的旅程；如果每个地方都敞开，那么到达任何地方就等于总算有了着落。

intro.en: Anywhere is a native compound of any and where, and where descends from the old interrogative word for place.
intro.cn: anywhere 是 any 与 where 的本族复合，而 where 源自古老的表示地点的疑问词。

items.en: Hwǣr meant 'at what place', and ǣnig 'any' was already ready to combine with question words.
items.cn: hwǣr 表示「在何处」，而 ǣnig「任何一个」早已可以和疑问词组合。

items.en: The two words appear together as any where, still written separately and meaning 'in any place'.
items.cn: 两个词并排出现，写作 any where，仍分开书写，义为「在任何地方」。

items.en: The spelling closes into anywhere, and the word settles in questions and negatives.
items.cn: 拼写合拢为 anywhere，这个词稳定出现在疑问句与否定句中。

items.en: The figurative phrase get anywhere develops, turning place into progress.
items.cn: 比喻性的短语 get anywhere 发展出来，把「地方」转成「进展」。

items.en: British and American pronunciation differ, but the spelling and meaning are the same on both sides.
items.cn: 英式与美式发音有别，但两边的拼写与含义一致。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the any-compounds; the near-meaning group gathers the place adverbs that divide the same map by sentence type.
note.cn: 形近组收 any 构成的复合词；近义组收表示地点的副词，它们按句式分摊同一张地图。

entries.definition: A pronoun meaning any person, built on the same any.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「任何人」，由同一个 any 构成。

entries.definition: A pronoun meaning any thing, used in the same sentence types.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「任何事物」，出现在相同的句式中。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in any way or in spite of that.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「以任何方式」或「无论如何」。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in spite of that, also used to close a topic.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「无论如何」，也用于收束话题。

entries.definition: In or to an unspecified place.
entries.definitionCN: 指某个未指明的地方，主要用于肯定句。

entries.definition: In or to every place, with no exception.
entries.definitionCN: 指每一个地方，没有例外，范围是全部而不是任意一处。

entries.definition: In or to no place at all, the negative partner of anywhere.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何地方都不，是 anywhere 的否定对应词。

entries.definition: An informal American synonym of anywhere.
entries.definitionCN: 美式口语中与 anywhere 同义的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real any-plus-where structure and the map-like range the word covers.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 any 加 where 结构，以及这个词覆盖的地图式范围。

normal.en: Any plus where: any single point on the map, name not needed.
normal.cn: any 加 where：地图上的任意一个点，不需要名字。

normal.en: Its home is the question and the denial: have you looked anywhere? I could not find it anywhere.
normal.cn: 它的家是疑问与否定：你找过哪儿吗？我哪儿都找不到。

normal.en: In statements it grants the whole map: sit anywhere you like.
normal.cn: 在陈述句里它把整张地图都放行：你想坐哪儿都行。

normal.en: The place family is regular: some, every, no, any plus where.
normal.cn: 地点这一族很规整：some、every、no、any 都接 where。

normal.en: Progress borrows the map: to get anywhere is to arrive at some result.
normal.cn: 「进展」借用了这张地图：get anywhere 就是终于到达某个结果。

abstract.en: Picture a finger hovering over a map, refusing to land on one town.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在地图上悬着，拒绝落在某一个城镇上。

abstract.en: The word is a map with no pin in it: every point is allowed.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一张没有插针的地图：每个点都被允许。

abstract.en: Under denial the map is folded shut, and no point remains visible.
abstract.cn: 在否定之下地图被折起合上，一个点也看不见了。

examples.en: Have you looked anywhere for the missing keys?
examples.cn: 你有没有到任何地方找过那串丢失的钥匙？

examples.en: The sound did not come from anywhere in the room.
examples.cn: 那声音不是从房间里的任何地方传来的。

examples.en: You can sit anywhere you like in the hall.
examples.cn: 大厅里你想坐哪儿都行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安妮威尔」——安妮摊开地图说「威尔，你去哪儿都行」：任何地方

root: anywhere 由 any「任何一个」与 where「何处」在本族英语中复合而成。古英语 hwǣr 表示「在何处」，ǣnig 可与疑问词组合；中古英语分写为 any where；十六世纪合拢为 anywhere，稳定用于疑问与否定；十九世纪发展出比喻义 get anywhere「取得进展」；现代英式与美式发音略异，拼写与含义一致。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses fan out from one open map: a denial that any point was reached, a question about which point was tried, a general permission covering every point, and the figurative journey towards progress.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法从一张敞开的地图展开：否认到达任何一点、询问试过哪一点、覆盖每一点的普遍许可，以及通往进展的比喻旅程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map spread wide, with no pin fixed in any one town.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张摊开的大地图，没有一枚图钉钉在某个城镇上。

branches.en: THE DENIAL LINE: the map is shut and no point on it counts.
branches.cn: 否定线：地图合上，上面没有一个点算数。

branches.en: THE QUESTION LINE: which point, if any, has already been tried?
branches.cn: 疑问线：到底试过哪个点，还是哪一点都没试过？

branches.en: THE PERMISSION LINE: every point on the map is open to the visitor.
branches.cn: 许可线：地图上的每一个点都向来者敞开。

branches.en: THE PROGRESS LINE: arriving anywhere means arriving at a result.
branches.cn: 进展线：到达任何地方，就意味着终于到了某个结果。

branches.en: THE FREE RANGE LINE: an open map grants both movement and outcome.
branches.cn: 自由范围线：敞开的地图同时给出行动与结果。

intro.en: Anywhere is transparent: any plus where, standing in the regular set with some, every and no.
intro.cn: anywhere 的构造透明：any 加 where，与 some、every、no 配成规整的一套。

latinIntro.en: Anywhere has no Latin source; Latin ubi and alicubi are functional parallels for place questions.
latinIntro.cn: anywhere 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语的 ubi 与 alicubi 只是地点疑问功能上的平行词。

definition_zh: 分开地；相隔；拆开；成碎片；除……之外；区别开
definition_en: separated by space or distance; also into pieces, or besides, as in apart from
core_image: 原本靠在一起的两件东西，被从中间掰开
scene: 老屋的院子里，两个工人把一张旧木桌的桌腿卸了下来。The two legs stood apart on the grass, waiting to be repaired.
sceneCN: 这里 apart 是「分开地」（第 1 个义项：两个原本相连的部分在空间上分离）；句意为「两条桌腿分开立在草地上，等着被修好」。画面里有老屋的院子、卸下的桌腿和蹲着检查的工人。

pos.zh: 副词：分开地；相隔；拆开；成碎片；除……之外

derivatives.zh: 借自南非荷兰语，与 apart 同源，义为「种族隔离制度」
由 apart 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，罕用，义为「分离的状态」

senses.title: Separated in space
senses.definition: so that two things are no longer together in the same place
senses.definitionCN: 使两件东西不再处在同一个地方
senses.example: The two legs stood apart on the grass, waiting to be repaired.
senses.exampleCN: 两条桌腿分开立在草地上，等着被修好。
senses.why: The French source means 'to one side'; once a thing is placed to one side, the pair that was together is visibly split.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意思是「放在一边」；一件东西被放到一边，原本合在一起的一对就明显分开了。

senses.title: At a distance from each other
senses.definition: used after a distance to say how far two places or things are from each other
senses.definitionCN: 用在距离之后，表示两个地方或两件东西相隔多远
senses.example: The two houses stand a hundred metres apart.
senses.exampleCN: 那两栋房子相隔一百米。
senses.why: Distance is separation measured: the gap created when things are put to one side can be counted in metres.
senses.whyCN: 距离是被量出来的分离：东西被放到一边后产生的空隙，可以用米来计数。

senses.title: Into pieces, out of order
senses.definition: in phrases such as take apart or fall apart, so that a whole is divided into its parts
senses.definitionCN: 用于 take apart 或 fall apart 一类短语，表示整体被分成若干部分
senses.example: The old chair fell apart when he sat on it.
senses.exampleCN: 他一坐上去，那把旧椅子就散架了。
senses.why: If a whole can be put to one side piece by piece, the parts end up separated, and the object is no longer one thing.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个整体可以被一件件放到一边，各部分最终就各自分离，这个物件也不再是一个整体。

senses.title: Besides, except for
senses.definition: in the phrase apart from, used to mean except for or in addition to
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 apart from，表示「除……之外」或「除了……还有」
senses.example: Apart from the noise, the hotel was comfortable.
senses.exampleCN: 除了有点吵，这家旅馆住着还算舒服。
senses.why: To set one item apart from the rest is to remove it from the group being judged, which is exactly what 'except' does.
senses.whyCN: 把一项从其余各项中分出去，就是把它从被评判的群体里移开，这恰好是「除……之外」所做的事。

senses.title: Distinguished from another
senses.definition: in the phrase tell apart, to recognize the difference between two similar things
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 tell apart，表示辨认出两个相似事物之间的差别
senses.example: The twins look so alike that few people can tell them apart.
senses.exampleCN: 这对双胞胎长得太像，很少有人能把他们分辨出来。
senses.why: Separating two things in the mind is the same gesture as separating them in space: first they stand apart, then they can be told apart.
senses.whyCN: 在心里分开两样东西，与在空间里分开它们是同一个动作：先在认识上立开，才能把它们分辨出来。

intro.en: Apart comes through Old French from Latin, and its oldest sense is 'placed to one side'.
intro.cn: apart 经古法语来自拉丁语，它最古老的义项是「被放在一边」。

items.en: The phrase ad partem meant 'to a part, to one side', built from ad 'to' and pars, partis 'part'.
items.cn: 短语 ad partem 表示「到一部分、到一边」，由 ad「向」与 pars、partis「部分」构成。

items.en: The phrase fuses into a part, literally 'to one side', and passes into English as a single adverb.
items.cn: 这个短语在古法语中融合为 a part，字面是「到一边」，随后作为一个副词进入英语。

items.en: The form apart is established with the sense 'separately, at a distance'.
items.cn: 形式 apart 确立下来，义为「分开地、相隔地」。

items.en: The 'into pieces' sense grows in phrases like take apart and fall apart, where a whole is divided.
items.cn: 「成碎片」义在 take apart 与 fall apart 一类短语里成长，整体被分成部分。

items.en: The compound preposition apart from is fixed, meaning both 'except' and 'besides'.
items.cn: 复合介词 apart from 定型，同时表示「除……之外」与「除了……还有」。

items.en: The word works mostly in phrases; its Latin root pars also gives part, partial and particle through other routes.
items.cn: 这个词主要活在短语里；它的拉丁词根 pars 还经其他路径给出了 part、partial、particle 等词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the shape or the root; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of separation and exception.
note.cn: 形近组收共享词形或词根的词；近义组收表示分离与排除的副词。

entries.definition: To or on one side, out of the main course.
entries.definitionCN: 到一边或在一边，偏出主要路线。

entries.definition: Far away in space or time.

entries.definition: Not including the one thing named.
entries.definitionCN: 不包括被点名的那一项，与 apart from 的排除义对应。

normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的法语与拉丁语来源，以及这个词实际栖身的短语。

normal.en: The source is 'to one side': put a thing aside and it is apart.
normal.cn: 来源义是「放到一边」：把东西放到一边，它就分开了。

normal.en: Distance is counted separation: two houses a hundred metres apart.

normal.en: Whole to pieces is the same move: take apart, fall apart.

normal.en: Set one item aside and you have apart from, meaning except.
normal.cn: 把一项放到一边，就得到 apart from，也就是「除……之外」。

normal.en: In the mind the same gap lets you tell two twins apart.
normal.cn: 在心里拉开同样的空隙，你就能把一对双胞胎分辨开。

abstract.en: Picture a seam being pulled open until the two halves stand on their own.
abstract.cn: 想象一条接缝被拉开，直到两半各自独立站着。

abstract.en: The word is a gap made visible: what was one becomes two.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一道被看见的空隙：原来的一件变成了两件。

abstract.en: In judgment the same gap becomes exception: everything except the one set aside.
abstract.cn: 在判断里，同样的空隙变成例外：除了被放到一边的那一个，其余都算。

root: apart 经古法语 a part 来自拉丁语短语 ad partem「到一部分、到一边」，由 ad「向」与 pars「部分」构成。中古英语确立为「分开地、相隔地」；十六至十七世纪在 take apart、fall apart 等短语里生出「成碎片」义；十八世纪复合介词 apart from 定型，兼表「除……之外」与「除了……还有」；现代主要活在短语中，其拉丁词根亦经其他路径给出 part、partial 等词。

sensesIntro.en: Five uses fan out from 'to one side': physical separation, measured distance, a whole divided into pieces, the exception set aside, and the mental gap that distinguishes two things.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个用法从「放到一边」展开：空间上的分离、被计量的距离、整体被分成碎片、被放到一边的例外，以及区分两物的心理空隙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seam pulled open until what was one whole stands as two.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条接缝被拉开，直到原本的一体站成两件。

branches.en: THE SEPARATION LINE: the pair no longer occupies one place.
branches.cn: 分离线：一对东西不再占据同一个地方。

branches.en: THE DISTANCE LINE: the gap is measured in metres or miles.
branches.cn: 距离线：那道空隙用米或英里来计量。

branches.en: THE PIECES LINE: the whole comes apart into its parts.
branches.cn: 碎片线：整体散成若干部分。

branches.en: THE EXCEPTION LINE: one item is set aside from the group.
branches.cn: 例外线：有一项被从群体中放到一边。

branches.en: THE JUDGMENT LINE: the same gap lets the mind tell two things apart.
branches.cn: 判断线：同样的空隙让心思把两样东西分辨开。

intro.en: Apart is a fossilized phrase rather than a fresh compound: Latin ad plus pars, worn down through French into one word.
intro.cn: apart 是一个凝固的短语，而不是新造的复合词：拉丁语 ad 加 pars，经法语磨成了一个词。

latinIntro.en: Here the Latin ancestry is real: ad 'to' and pars 'part' are the actual source of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 这里的拉丁语血统是真的：ad「向」与 pars「部分」正是这个英语词的实际来源。

definition_zh: 公寓套房；一套住房；公寓楼中的单元
definition_en: a set of rooms for living in, usually within a larger building and often rented
core_image: 从一栋大房子里切出的一套独立房间
scene: 老城区的砖楼里，房东打开一扇刷成绿色的门。The apartment on the third floor has two windows facing the river.
sceneCN: 这里 apartment 是「公寓套房」（第 1 个义项：一栋楼里供人居住的一整套房间）；句意为「三楼那套公寓有两扇窗朝着河」。画面里有老城区的砖楼、刷成绿色的门和站在门口的房东。

senses.title: A set of rooms to live in
senses.definition: a self-contained set of rooms used as a home, usually inside a larger building
senses.definitionCN: 一整套自成一体的居住房间，通常位于一栋更大的楼房之内
senses.example: The apartment on the third floor has two windows facing the river.
senses.exampleCN: 三楼那套公寓有两扇窗朝着河。
senses.why: The Italian source is built on 'apart': the set of rooms is literally a portion separated off from the rest of the building.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语来源建立在「分开」之上：这一整套房间字面上就是从整栋楼里分出来的一份。

senses.title: A rented dwelling
senses.definition: such a set of rooms when it is rented rather than owned
senses.definitionCN: 指上述成套房间在用于出租而非自有时的情况
senses.example: They rented a small apartment above the bakery.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在面包店楼上租了一套小公寓。
senses.why: English usage narrows the borrowed word towards urban renting, so the separated set of rooms is typically someone else's property.
senses.whyCN: 英语用法把这个借词收窄到城市租房，于是这套分出来的房间通常属于别人。

senses.title: A unit within a building
senses.definition: one numbered or lettered unit among many in the same residential building
senses.definitionCN: 同一栋住宅楼里众多单元中带编号或字母的那一个
senses.example: The apartment building has a shared garden at the back.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋公寓楼后面有一个共用的花园。
senses.why: The building is the whole and each apartment is a part, which is exactly the 'part' image inside the Latin root.
senses.whyCN: 整栋楼是整体，每一套公寓是部分，这正是拉丁词根内部那个「部分」的意象。

senses.title: A private set of rooms in a large house
senses.titleCN: 大宅中的一套私用房间
senses.definition: in older British use, a private suite of rooms within a large house
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的英式用法，指大宅内部供私人使用的一整套房间
senses.example: The family kept a separate apartment in the east wing.
senses.exampleCN: 那家人在东翼保留了一套独立的房间。
senses.why: Before the word meant a rented city flat, it named any rooms cut off for private use inside a greater house.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词指城市出租公寓之前，它指的是大宅内部为私人使用而切出来的任何一组房间。

intro.en: Apartment is a Romance borrowing whose root means 'separated', so the word has always carried the idea of a part cut off from a whole.
intro.cn: apartment 是罗曼语借词，词根意为「分开」，所以这个词始终带着「从整体中切出一部分」的意思。

items.en: Pars, partis meant 'part', and the phrase ad partem 'to one side' lies behind the verb appartare 'to separate'.
items.cn: pars、partis 表示「部分」，而短语 ad partem「到一边」正是动词 appartare「分开」的背后来源。

items.en: Appartamento names a set of rooms set apart for a person or family, built directly on appartare.
items.cn: appartamento 指为某人或某家庭分出来的一套房间，直接由 appartare 构成。

items.en: French takes the word as appartement and uses it for a private set of rooms in a large house.
items.cn: 法语借入为 appartement，用来指大宅中供私人使用的一整套房间。

items.en: English borrows apartment with the French sense of private rooms rather than a rented city dwelling.
items.cn: 英语借入 apartment 时，取的是法语「私人成套房间」的义项，而不是城市出租住处。

items.en: With the growth of cities the word shifts towards the modern rented flat inside a residential block.
items.cn: 随着城市扩张，这个词转向现代意义上住宅楼里的出租套房。

items.en: American usage prefers apartment where British usage often says flat; the building compounds are fixed on both sides.
items.cn: 美式用法偏爱 apartment，而英式常用 flat；两边与楼宇相关的复合词都已定型。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same 'part, separate' root; the near-meaning group gathers other names for a dwelling.
note.cn: 形近组收同出「部分、分开」词根的词；近义组收其他表示住处的名称。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real 'separated part' root and the building compounds the word forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的「分出一部分」词根，以及这个词构成的楼宇复合词。

normal.en: The root says 'apart': an apartment is a part cut off from the whole building.
normal.cn: 词根说的是「分开」：apartment 就是从整栋楼里切出来的一部分。

normal.en: Think of one flat sliced out of a block, with its own door and windows.

normal.cn: 美式 apartment 等于英式 flat，两者都指大建筑里的一处住处。

normal.en: The compounds are easy: apartment building, apartment block, apartment hotel.

abstract.en: Picture a cake sliced neatly: each apartment is one slice with its own icing.
abstract.cn: 想象一块被切得整齐的蛋糕：每套公寓就是一片，各自带自己的糖霜。

abstract.en: The word is a boundary drawn inside a building: outside is the street, inside is a life.
abstract.cn: 这个词是在一栋楼里画下的一条界线：外面是街道，里面是一段生活。

abstract.en: Separation is the point: one roof, many private worlds.
abstract.cn: 分离才是要点：一个屋顶之下，许多个私人的世界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one flat slice cut neatly out of a larger building, with its own door.

branches.en: THE RENTAL LINE: the separated rooms belong to a landlord.
branches.cn: 出租线：这套分出来的房间属于房东。

branches.en: THE UNIT LINE: one numbered part among many under one roof.
branches.cn: 单元线：同一个屋顶下众多编号部分中的一个。

branches.en: THE OLD SUITE LINE: rooms cut off for private use in a great house.

definition_en: to say that one is sorry for something one has done; in older use, to speak in defense of a position

senses.title: To say one is sorry
senses.definition: to tell someone that one is sorry for a fault, mistake, or harm one has caused
senses.definitionCN: 告诉某人自己为造成的过失、错误或伤害感到抱歉
senses.example: He apologized for breaking the plate before she could say a word.
senses.exampleCN: 在母亲开口之前，他就为打碎盘子道了歉。
senses.why: The Greek source meant a speech of defense; the modern verb keeps the speech but drops the defense, leaving only the admission of fault.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源指一篇辩护的言辞；现代动词保留了「言辞」，却去掉了「辩护」，只剩下对过失的承认。

senses.title: To make amends in words
senses.definition: to offer words of regret as a way of repairing a broken relationship
senses.definitionCN: 用表示懊悔的话来修补一段受损的关系
senses.example: You should apologize to her at once.
senses.exampleCN: 你应该马上向她赔个不是。
senses.why: An apology is a small ritual of repair: words stand in for the damage that cannot simply be undone.
senses.whyCN: 道歉是一种小小的修补仪式：用言语代替那些无法直接撤销的损害。

senses.title: To apologize publicly
senses.definition: to state regret openly, often in public or on behalf of an organization
senses.definitionCN: 公开表达歉意，常指在公众场合或代表某个机构致歉
senses.example: The company apologized publicly for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 公司为这次延误公开道了歉。
senses.why: When the fault is public, the repair must also be public; the same speech is now performed before witnesses.
senses.whyCN: 当过失是公开的，修补也必须公开；同一番言辞如今要在众人面前说出。

senses.title: To speak in defense, old use
senses.definition: in older and formal use, to argue in defense of a belief, person, or institution
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧与正式的用法中，为某种信念、人物或机构辩护
senses.example: The old essay apologizes for the customs of its age.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇旧文为它那个时代的习俗作辩护。
senses.why: This is the original Greek sense surviving in formal prose, where the speech is still a shield rather than a confession.
senses.whyCN: 这是希腊语本义在正式散文中的残留，那里的言辞仍是一面盾牌，而不是一份认错书。

intro.en: Apologize descends from a Greek word for a speech of defense, so its oldest meaning is the opposite of the modern confession.
intro.cn: apologize 源自希腊语中表示「辩护之辞」的词，因此它最古老的含义与现代的认错恰好相反。

items.en: Apologia was a speech made in defense, built from apo- 'away from' and logos 'word, speech, account'.
items.cn: apologia 是为辩护而作的言辞，由 apo-「离开」与 logos「言词、说法」构成。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as apologia, keeping the sense of a formal defense or justification.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 apologia，保留「正式辩护或申辩」的义项。

items.en: English takes apology in the learned sense of a defense, and the word belongs to theology and rhetoric.
items.cn: 英语借入 apology 时取的是学术意义上的「辩护」，这个词属于神学与修辞学。

items.en: The verb apologize appears with the modern sense 'to say one is sorry', while the noun keeps both defense and regret.
items.cn: 动词 apologize 出现，取现代义「表示抱歉」，而名词则同时保留辩护与歉意两种含义。

items.en: The confessional sense dominates everyday use, and the defensive sense retreats into apologist and formal prose.
items.cn: 认错义在日常使用中占主导，辩护义退入 apologist 一词与正式散文里。

items.en: The everyday verb means simply 'say sorry'; its Greek skeleton is visible mainly in the derived nouns.
items.cn: 日常动词的意思就是「说抱歉」；它的希腊骨架主要还能在派生名词里看见。

note.cn: 形近组收由它派生的一族词；近义组收承认过失或作出弥补的动词。

abstract.en: Public apology adds witnesses: the bridge is built in the open, for everyone to see.

senses.title: A statement of regret
senses.definition: words or a written message saying that one is sorry for a fault or harm
senses.definitionCN: 口头或书面的言辞，表示为某项过失或伤害感到抱歉
senses.example: Her apology was a hand-written note tied to a bunch of white roses.
senses.exampleCN: 她的道歉是一张绑在一束白玫瑰上的手写便条。
senses.why: The Greek word named a defense speech, but the modern noun has dropped the defense and kept only the regret, so the statement itself becomes the amends.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词原本指辩护之辞，但现代名词丢掉了辩护，只留下懊悔，于是这番陈述本身就成了补偿。

senses.title: An accepted repair of a relationship
senses.definition: such a statement considered as a social act that restores good relations
senses.definitionCN: 把这类言辞视为一种恢复良好关系的社会行为
senses.example: She accepted his apology with a quiet nod.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻轻点头，接受了他的道歉。
senses.why: An apology is a small ritual: since the damage cannot be undone, words are offered and then accepted in its place.
senses.whyCN: 道歉是一种小仪式：既然损害无法撤销，就用言辞顶上去，再被对方接受。

senses.title: A formal defense, old use
senses.definition: in older and formal use, a written or spoken defense of a person, belief, or institution
senses.definitionCN: 较旧与正式的用法，指为人、信念或机构所作的书面或口头辩护
senses.example: The book is an apology for the old system of guilds.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是为旧的行会制度作辩白。
senses.why: This is the original Greek sense, still visible in titles and in the derived word apologist, where the speech is a shield.
senses.whyCN: 这是希腊语本义，仍见于书名与派生词 apologist 之中，那里的言辞是一面盾牌。

senses.title: A poor substitute
senses.definition: in informal and often ironic use, something that is a very inadequate example or replacement
senses.definitionCN: 非正式且常带反讽的用法，指极不像样的事物或替代品
senses.example: The so-called garden was a poor apology for a park.
senses.exampleCN: 那座所谓的花园，勉强算个公园的替代品。
senses.why: The ironic sense grows by contrast: a mere word standing in for a real thing is as weak as an apology standing in for repair.
senses.whyCN: 这个反讽义靠对比生长：仅用言辞顶替实物，就像用道歉顶替修补一样无力。

senses.title: A public or official statement
senses.definition: an official statement of regret issued by an institution or a person in public
senses.definitionCN: 由机构或个人在公众场合发布的正式致歉声明
senses.example: The airline issued a public apology for the cancelled flights.
senses.exampleCN: 航空公司为取消的航班发布了公开道歉。
senses.why: When the fault is public, the repair must be public too, so the private word of regret becomes an official document.
senses.whyCN: 当过失是公开的，修补也必须公开，于是私下的懊悔之言变成一份正式文件。

intro.en: Apology comes from a Greek word for a speech of defense, and its modern sense of regret is a later turning of that word.
intro.cn: apology 来自希腊语中表示「辩护之辞」的词，它现代的「歉意」义是后来转出来的。

items.en: Apologia meant a speech in defense, built from apo- 'away from' and logos 'word, account'; Plato's defense of Socrates bore this name.
items.cn: apologia 指为辩护而作的言辞，由 apo-「离开」与 logos「言词、论述」构成；柏拉图那篇为苏格拉底辩护的文字就叫这个名字。

items.en: Latin keeps apologia as a learned word for a formal defense or justification.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留 apologia，作为表示正式辩护或申辩的学术词。

items.en: English borrows apology in the sense 'defense', and the word is at home in theology and rhetoric.
items.cn: 英语借入 apology 时取「辩护」义，这个词在神学与修辞学里安家。

items.en: The sense shifts towards 'expression of regret', while the old defensive sense survives in set titles and in apologist.
items.cn: 词义转向「表达歉意」，而旧的辩护义保留在固定书名与 apologist 一词里。

items.en: The ironic sense 'poor substitute' appears in informal writing, often with the phrase an apology for.
items.cn: 反讽的「不像样的替代品」义出现在非正式文字里，常与短语 an apology for 连用。

items.en: The everyday meaning is simply 'a statement of regret'; the other senses are marked as formal, historical, or ironic.
items.cn: 日常含义就是「致歉的言辞」；其余义项则被标为正式、历史或反讽用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived family; the near-meaning group gathers words for regret, defense and substitute.
note.cn: 形近组收由它派生的一族词；近义组收表示懊悔、辩护与替代品的词。

examples.en: She accepted his apology with a quiet nod.
examples.cn: 她轻轻点头，接受了他的道歉。

examples.en: The manager offered a sincere apology to every guest.
examples.cn: 经理向每位客人真诚地道了歉。

examples.en: His apology for the mistake arrived a week too late.
examples.cn: 他为那次错误所作的道歉晚了一周才到。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额怕了债」——打碎东西怕被追债，赶紧递上一张写满对不起的便条：道歉

root: apology 来自希腊语 apologia「辩护之辞」，由 apo-「离开」与 logos「言词、论述」构成，经拉丁语 apologia 进入英语。十六世纪英语仍取「辩护」义，用于神学与修辞；十八世纪转向「表达歉意」，旧义退守固定书名与 apologist；十九世纪出现反讽义「不像样的替代品」，常作 an apology for；现代日常义就是「致歉的言辞」。

sensesIntro.en: Five uses fan out from a defense speech that became a confession: the spoken regret, the social repair, the old defense, the ironic substitute, and the official public statement.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个用法从一篇转为认错的辩护之辞展开：口头的懊悔、社会性的修补、旧的辩护义、反讽的替代品，以及正式的公开声明。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a defense speech lowered into a confession, then handed over like a note.
core.cn: 核心意象：一篇辩护之辞被放低成认错，再像便条一样递出去。

branches.en: THE REGRET LINE: the defense is gone and only sorrow remains.
branches.cn: 懊悔线：辩护没有了，只剩歉意。

branches.en: THE REPAIR LINE: words are offered and accepted in place of damage.
branches.cn: 修补线：用言辞顶替损害，并被对方接受。

branches.en: THE OLD SHIELD LINE: the Greek defense survives in titles and in apologist.
branches.cn: 旧盾牌线：希腊语的辩护义活在书名与 apologist 里。

branches.en: THE IRONY LINE: a word pretending to be a thing is a poor apology for it.
branches.cn: 反讽线：一个假装成实物的词，就是它勉强的替代品。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC LINE: private regret becomes an official document.
branches.cn: 公开线：私下的懊悔变成一份正式文件。

intro.en: Apology is a classical borrowing, so its parts are Greek and Latin rather than native English.
intro.cn: apology 是古典借词，因此它的构件来自希腊语与拉丁语，而非本族英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin link is direct: apologia carried the Greek word into English, and the derived family keeps the same skeleton.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语这一环是直接的：apologia 把这个希腊词带进英语，派生的一族保留着同样的骨架。

items.meaning: a defense speech; now a statement of regret
items.example: The note was a simple apology.
items.exampleCN: 那张便条是一句简单的道歉。

items.example: It turns the speech away from the charge.
items.exampleCN: 它把言辞从指控那里转开。

items.example: Logos gives the word its speaking core.
items.exampleCN: logos 提供了这个词言说的核心。

items.example: He came to apologize in person.
items.exampleCN: 他亲自来道歉。

items.example: Her tone was apologetic.
items.exampleCN: 她的语气带着歉意。

items.example: He smiled apologetically and stepped aside.
items.exampleCN: 他带着歉意笑了笑，让到一边。

items.example: The apologist defended the old treaty.
items.exampleCN: 那位辩护者为旧条约辩护。

items.example: It appears in words such as biology.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 biology 这类词里。

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词的后缀，表示「与……有关的」
items.example: It turns the noun into an adjective of manner.
items.exampleCN: 它把名词变成表示态度的形容词。

latinEntries.example: Apologia is the immediate source of apology.
latinEntries.exampleCN: apologia 是 apology 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 明显的；显而易见的；表面上的；貌似的
definition_en: easy to see or understand; also seeming rather than certainly true
core_image: 东西浮到表面，一眼就看见，却未必是全部
scene: 清晨的湖面起了薄雾，岸边的船影慢慢清晰起来。It became apparent that the ferry would not sail that day.
sceneCN: 这里 apparent 是「明显的」（第 1 个义项：事情变得清楚，一眼就能看出来）；句意为「情况变得很明显，那天渡轮不会开航」。画面里有清晨的湖面、薄雾和渐渐清晰的船影。

pos.zh: 形容词：明显的；显而易见的；表面上的；貌似的

collocations.zh: 法定继承人；公认的接班者

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「显然；据说」
与本词同出拉丁语 apparere，义为「出现；显得」
由同一拉丁词根 apparere 派生，义为「幽灵；幻影」

senses.title: Easy to see or understand
senses.definition: clearly visible or easily understood, so that no doubt remains
senses.definitionCN: 清楚可见或容易理解，以至于不再有疑问
senses.example: It became apparent that the ferry would not sail that day.
senses.exampleCN: 情况变得很明显，那天渡轮不会开航。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'come into sight'; what has come into sight is no longer hidden, which is precisely the sense of 'obvious'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词本义是「进入视野」；进入视野的东西不再被遮住，这正是「显而易见」的意思。

senses.title: Seeming rather than certain
senses.definition: appearing to be true on the surface, though it may not be so in reality
senses.definitionCN: 表面上看来如此，实际上未必如此
senses.example: The apparent calm of the town hid a great deal of worry.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇表面上的平静掩盖了许多忧虑。
senses.why: The same word that reports what is seen can also warn that only the surface has been seen, so 'apparent' comes to mark a possible illusion.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既能报告所见，也能提醒所见只是表面，于是 apparent 转而标记一种可能的假象。

senses.title: Visible to the eye
senses.definition: able to be seen, especially in astronomy for a star or planet visible without aid
senses.definitionCN: 能够被看见，尤用于天文学，指无需仪器即可看见的恒星或行星
senses.example: The comet is apparent to the naked eye only before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 那颗彗星只有在天亮前才能用肉眼看见。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical layer: before the word meant 'obvious' it simply meant 'showing itself to sight'.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的具体层：在表示「明显」之前，它只是「把自己显给视觉看」的意思。

senses.title: Undisputed, as in heir apparent
senses.titleCN: 确定的；无可争议的（用于 heir apparent）
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase heir apparent, clearly next in line and not to be displaced by a later claimant
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定短语 heir apparent，指明确排在下一位、不会被后来者取代的继承者
senses.example: She was the heir apparent to the old bookstore.
senses.exampleCN: 她是那家旧书店公认的接班人。
senses.why: If a right is apparent to everyone, it is beyond dispute; the legal phrase borrows that clarity for succession.
senses.whyCN: 如果一项权利对所有人都显而易见，它就无可争议；这个法律短语把这份清楚借给了继承次序。

intro.en: Apparent comes from a Latin verb meaning 'come into sight', so its oldest sense is visual rather than logical.
intro.cn: apparent 来自一个表示「进入视野」的拉丁动词，因此它最古老的义项是视觉的，而不是逻辑的。

items.en: Apparere meant 'come into view, show oneself', built from ad- 'to' and parere 'come forth, be visible'.
items.cn: apparere 表示「进入视野、显现自身」，由 ad-「向」与 parere「出现、可见」构成。

items.en: The present participle aparant 'being visible' passes into English as an adjective.
items.cn: 现在分词 aparant「可见的、显现的」作为形容词进入英语。

items.en: English apparent first means 'visible, manifest', used of things that can be seen with the eyes.
items.cn: 英语 apparent 最初义为「可见的、显现的」，用于可以用眼睛看见的事物。

items.en: The sense widens from sight to understanding: what is plainly seen becomes what is plainly understood.
items.cn: 词义从视觉扩展到理解：看得清楚的东西变成理解得清楚的东西。

items.en: The qualifying sense 'seeming, not necessarily real' develops, often in contrast with 'actual'.
items.cn: 限定性的「表面上、未必真实」义发展出来，常与 actual 形成对照。

items.en: Both senses coexist: apparent facts are clear, while apparent calm may be only on the surface.
items.cn: 两种义项并存：apparent facts 是清楚的事实，而 apparent calm 可能只停留在表面。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the family from the same Latin verb; the near-meaning group gathers words for clarity and for mere appearance.
note.cn: 形近组收同出那个拉丁动词的一族词；近义组收表示清楚与仅止于表面的词。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning seemingly, or as far as one can tell.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「看来；据说」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to come into sight or to seem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「出现；显得」，与本词同出拉丁语 apparere。

entries.definition: A noun meaning the act of appearing or the look of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「出现；外表」，同出 apparere 这一词根。

entries.definition: A noun meaning a ghostly figure that suddenly appears.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幽灵、幻影」，指突然显现的身影。

entries.definition: So clear that it needs no explanation or effort to see.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚到不需要解释或费力去看，语气比 apparent 更直接。

entries.definition: Clear from the evidence, often in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 由证据而显得清楚，常见于正式文字，语气比 apparent 更书面。

entries.definition: Appearing to be true without being proved so.
entries.definitionCN: 看来如此却未被证实，与 apparent 的「表面上」义最接近。

entries.definition: Stated or shown outwardly, often with a hint of doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 对外宣称或显示的，常暗含怀疑，比 apparent 更强调「名义上的」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real 'come into sight' verb and the two opposite directions the adjective took.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的「进入视野」动词，以及这个形容词走出的两个相反方向。

normal.en: The core verb means 'come into sight': what appears is what can be seen.
normal.cn: 核心动词意为「进入视野」：显现出来的，就是能看见的。

normal.en: From sight it moves to understanding: apparent facts are plain facts.
normal.cn: 从视觉转到理解：apparent facts 就是明摆着的事实。

normal.en: Then it learns to hedge: apparent calm may be only on the surface.
normal.cn: 然后它学会留余地：apparent calm 可能只停留在表面。

normal.en: The fixed frame is it became apparent that, followed by a clause.
normal.cn: 固定句式是 it became apparent that，后面接一个从句。

normal.en: The legal phrase heir apparent keeps the 'undisputed' edge.
normal.cn: 法律短语 heir apparent 保留了「无可争议」的锋利。

abstract.en: Picture an object rising to the surface of dark water and catching the light.
abstract.cn: 想象一件东西从深水里浮到水面，被光一照。

abstract.en: The word is a surface, not a depth: it shows what can be seen, not what is hidden below.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一个表面而不是深处：它展示看得见的，而不是藏在下头的。

abstract.en: Hence the double edge: what is apparent may be the whole truth or only its skin.
abstract.cn: 由此生出双刃：apparent 的东西可能是全部真相，也可能只是它的表皮。

examples.en: It soon became apparent that no one had brought the key.
examples.cn: 很快就明显看出，没有人带钥匙。

examples.en: The apparent calm of the town hid a great deal of worry.
examples.cn: 小镇表面上的平静掩盖了许多忧虑。

examples.en: For no apparent reason, the lights went out.
examples.cn: 没有任何明显理由，灯就灭了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额怕认特」——雾散船影显现，他说「怕认错，先看清」：明显的

root: apparent 经古法语 aparant 来自拉丁语 apparere「进入视野、显现」，该动词由 ad-「向」与 parere「出现、可见」构成。十四世纪英语义为「可见的、显现的」；十六世纪由视觉扩展到理解，义为「明显的」；十七世纪发展出「表面上、未必真实」的限定义，常与 actual 对照；现代两种义项并存，并有固定短语 heir apparent。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses fan out from 'come into sight': the plainly visible fact, the surface that may deceive, the astronomical object seen by eye, and the undisputed successor.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法从「进入视野」展开：明摆着的事实、可能骗人的表面、肉眼可见的天体，以及无可争议的接班人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something rising to the surface and catching the light, while the depth stays unseen.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物浮到表面被光照见，而深处仍看不见。

branches.en: THE CLARITY LINE: what has appeared is no longer in doubt.
branches.cn: 清楚线：已经显现的东西不再令人怀疑。

branches.en: THE SURFACE LINE: only the skin has been seen, so truth is still open.
branches.cn: 表面线：只看见了表皮，真相仍悬着。

branches.en: THE EYE LINE: the oldest sense, visible without aid.
branches.cn: 肉眼线：最古老的义项，无需仪器即可看见。

branches.en: THE SUCCESSION LINE: a right clear to all cannot be disputed.
branches.cn: 继承线：对所有人都清楚的权利，无法被争辩。

branches.en: THE DOUBLE EDGE LINE: the same word certifies and cautions.
branches.cn: 双刃线：同一个词既作担保，也作提醒。

intro.en: Apparent is a Latin borrowing, and its parts are the prefix ad- and the verb parere 'come forth'.
intro.cn: apparent 是拉丁语借词，它的构件是前缀 ad- 与动词 parere「出现」。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestry is direct: apparere is the verb behind apparent, appear and apparition.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语血统是直接的：apparere 正是 apparent、appear 与 apparition 背后的动词。

items.example: The reason for the delay was apparent to all.
items.exampleCN: 延误的原因对所有人都很明显。

items.example: The verb is the common root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的共同词根。

items.example: It directs the appearing towards the viewer.
items.exampleCN: 它把「显现」指向观看者。

items.example: Parere supplies the visible half of the word.
items.exampleCN: parere 提供了这个词中「可见」的那一半。

items.example: A light appeared on the far shore.
items.exampleCN: 远岸出现了一点灯光。

items.meaning: the act of appearing; outward look
items.example: The building has a plain appearance.
items.exampleCN: 这栋楼外表朴素。

items.meaning: seemingly; as far as one can tell
items.example: Apparently the train was cancelled.
items.exampleCN: 看来那趟火车被取消了。

items.meaningCN: 突然显现的幽灵或幻影
items.example: An apparition stood at the end of the corridor.
items.exampleCN: 走廊尽头立着一个幻影。

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词的后缀，表示「处于某种状态」
items.example: It turns the verb into a state of being visible.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成「处于可见状态」的形容词。

latinEntries.example: Apparere is the direct source of apparent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: apparere 是 apparent 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Parere sits inside the longer verb.
latinEntries.exampleCN: parere 嵌在那个更长的动词里。

definition_zh: 看来；显然；据说；表面上
definition_en: as far as one can see or judge; reportedly; seemingly, though not certainly
core_image: 从表面看得出的样子，却给自己留了余地
scene: 清晨的咖啡馆里，店员看了一眼空着的餐台。Apparently the delivery van broke down on the way.
sceneCN: 这里 apparently 是「看来」（第 1 个义项：根据眼前可见的情况作出判断，但语气留有余地）；句意为「看来送货车在半路上抛锚了」。画面里有清晨的咖啡馆、空着的餐台和望向门外的店员。

pos.zh: 副词：看来；显然；据说；表面上

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「明显的；表面上的」
与本词同出拉丁语 apparere，义为「出现；显得」
同出 apparere 这一词根的名词，义为「出现；外表」

senses.title: As far as one can tell
senses.definition: used to say that something seems to be true from the evidence available, without claiming certainty
senses.definitionCN: 表示根据手头可见的证据，某事看来为真，但不宣称确定
senses.example: Apparently the delivery van broke down on the way.
senses.exampleCN: 看来送货车在半路上抛锚了。
senses.why: The adjective means 'visible'; the adverb says that what is visible is all one has to go on, so the claim is made from the surface only.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义为「可见的」；副词则表示可见的东西就是全部依据，因此这个判断只从表面作出。

senses.title: Reportedly, according to others
senses.definition: used to report what other people say, especially when the speaker cannot confirm it personally
senses.definitionCN: 用于转述别人的说法，尤其是说话人自己无法亲自证实时
senses.example: Apparently the whole street lost power for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 据说整条街停了两个小时的电。
senses.why: Once 'what appears' can come from hearsay as well as from sight, the adverb becomes a polite way of quoting the town without vouching for it.
senses.whyCN: 当「显现出来的东西」也可以来自传闻而不只是亲眼所见，这个副词就变成一种得体的转述方式，替街坊传话却不作担保。

senses.title: Seemingly, but perhaps not really
senses.definition: used to describe how something looks while hinting that the reality may be different
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述某事物的外观，同时暗示实际情况可能不同
senses.example: She was apparently unaware of the new rule.
senses.exampleCN: 她看来并不知道这条新规定。
senses.why: The word can also warn: if only the surface has been read, the appearance may be a mask rather than the fact.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能起提醒作用：如果只读了表面，那副样子就可能是面具而不是事实。

senses.title: To soften a statement
senses.definition: used in conversation to make an assertion less direct or less confrontational
senses.definitionCN: 用于谈话中，使断言不那么直接、不那么咄咄逼人
senses.example: Apparently, we are expected to bring our own cups.
senses.exampleCN: 看样子，我们要自己带杯子。
senses.why: By attributing the claim to appearance rather than to oneself, the speaker avoids sounding blunt while still passing the message on.
senses.whyCN: 把断言归给「表面现象」而不是归给自己，说话人既能不显得生硬，又把话传了出去。

intro.en: Apparently is the adverb of apparent, built on a Latin verb meaning 'come into sight' plus the native suffix -ly.
intro.cn: apparently 是 apparent 的副词形式，由表示「进入视野」的拉丁动词加上本族后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: Apparere 'come into view' is built from ad- 'to' and parere 'come forth'; its participle apparans yields the adjective.
items.cn: apparere「进入视野」由 ad-「向」与 parere「出现」构成；它的分词 apparans 给出了形容词。

items.en: The participle aparant passes into English as apparent, and English later adds its own adverb suffix.
items.cn: 分词 aparant 作为 apparent 进入英语，英语后来又给它加上自己的副词后缀。

items.en: Apparently is recorded first in the sense 'evidently, plainly', close to the adjective's 'visible' sense.
items.cn: apparently 最初有记载的义项是「明显地、明白地」，接近形容词「可见的」义。

items.en: The reporting sense 'so people say' becomes common in newspapers and conversation.
items.cn: 转述义「听人说」在报纸与谈话中变得常见。

items.en: The adverb now mostly hedges: it presents a claim as seeming rather than certain, and often softens the sentence.
items.cn: 现代这个副词主要起留余地的作用：把断言呈现为「看来」而非确定，并常用来缓和语气。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the family from the same Latin verb; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs that hedge or report.
note.cn: 形近组收同出那个拉丁动词的一族词；近义组收表示留余地或转述的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning clearly visible or merely seeming.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明显的」或「表面上的」，本词由它加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to come into sight or to seem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「出现；显得」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A noun meaning the act of appearing or the outward look.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「出现；外表」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A noun meaning a ghostly figure that appears.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幽灵、幻影」，同出此词根。

entries.definition: Clearly, judging from the evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 根据证据来看显然如此，语气比 apparently 更肯定。

entries.definition: According to what has been reported, not confirmed by the speaker.
entries.definitionCN: 据报导、据传，明确表示来自转述，与 apparently 的「据说」义最近。

entries.definition: As it appears, often with a hint that the appearance may mislead.
entries.definitionCN: 看来如此，常暗示表象可能误导，与 apparently 的「表面上」义接近。

entries.definition: According to outward claim, often with doubt implied.
entries.definitionCN: 据对外宣称如此，常暗含怀疑，比 apparently 更强调「名义上」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real 'visible' root and the hedging positions the adverb takes in a sentence.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的「可见」词根，以及这个副词在句中留余地时的位置。

normal.en: The adjective means 'visible'; the adverb says that is all you have to go on.
normal.cn: 形容词义为「可见的」；副词则说这就是你手里的全部依据。

normal.en: Put it at the front to report: apparently, the van broke down.
normal.cn: 放在句首表示转述：看来，送货车抛锚了。

normal.en: It hedges a claim without denying it: apparently safe, but check first.
normal.cn: 它给断言留余地却不否认：看来安全，但先核实一下。

normal.en: It also softens: apparently, we need our own cups.
normal.cn: 它还能缓和语气：看样子，我们要自己带杯子。

normal.en: The family is regular: apparent, appear, appearance, apparition.
normal.cn: 这一族很规整：apparent、appear、appearance、apparition。

abstract.en: Picture a surface catching light while the depths below stay dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一个表面被光照亮，而下方的深处仍然发暗。

abstract.en: The word is a hand pointing at what is seen, with the other hand raised in caution.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一只手指出所见之物，另一只手同时抬起表示谨慎。

abstract.en: It keeps a door open: the sentence can always be revised when facts arrive.
abstract.cn: 它留着一扇门：等事实到来时，这句话随时可以修正。

examples.en: Apparently the delivery van broke down on the way.
examples.cn: 看来送货车在半路上抛锚了。

examples.en: She was apparently unaware of the new rule.
examples.cn: 她看来并不知道这条新规定。

examples.en: The path is apparently safe, though the map is old.
examples.cn: 这条路看来是安全的，尽管地图已经很旧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额怕认特利」——餐台空了，店员说「特地利索地送来了？看来没有」：看来

root: apparently 由 apparent 加本族副词后缀 -ly 构成，而 apparent 经古法语 aparant 来自拉丁语 apparere「进入视野、显现」，该动词由 ad-「向」与 parere「出现、可见」构成。十六世纪最初义为「明显地」；十九世纪在报纸与谈话中发展出「据说」的转述义；现代主要用来留余地，把断言呈现为「看来」而非确定。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses fan out from the surface of what is seen: a judgment from available evidence, a report from others, a warning that appearance may deceive, and a conversational softener.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法从所见之物的表面展开：根据现有证据的判断、转述他人的说法、提醒表象可能骗人，以及谈话中的缓和用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit surface above dark depths, read with one hand raised in caution.
core.cn: 核心意象：深处黑暗之上的一片受光表面，一只手边读边抬起示警。

chain: AS FAR AS ONE CAN TELL

branches.en: THE SURFACE LINE: the conclusion is drawn from what can be seen.
branches.cn: 表面线：结论取自看得见的部分。

branches.en: THE REPORT LINE: the evidence is what other people say.
branches.cn: 转述线：证据来自别人所说的话。

branches.en: THE WARNING LINE: appearance may be a mask, not the fact.
branches.cn: 警示线：表象可能是面具，而不是事实。

branches.en: THE SOFTENER LINE: the claim is passed on without a hard edge.
branches.cn: 缓和线：断言被传出去，却不带坚硬的棱角。

branches.en: THE HEDGE LINE: both hearsay and appearance keep certainty at arm's length.
branches.cn: 留余地线：传闻与表象都把确定性挡在一臂之外。

intro.en: Apparently is a hybrid: a Latin-rooted adjective plus the native English adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: apparently 是混合体：拉丁词根的形容词加上本族英语副词后缀 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is genuine: apparere is the verb behind the adjective, and parere sits inside that verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是真实的：apparere 是形容词背后的动词，而 parere 又嵌在那个动词里。

items.example: Apparently the shop opens late on Mondays.
items.exampleCN: 看来这家店周一开得晚。

items.example: The damage was apparent at once.
items.exampleCN: 损坏一眼就能看出来。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表示方式的副词。

items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整族词的根。

items.example: Parere gives the verb its visible core.
items.exampleCN: parere 提供了动词中「可见」的核心。

items.example: Stars appear one by one at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 黄昏时星星一颗颗出现。

items.meaning: the act of appearing; outward look
items.example: His appearance at the door surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 他出现在门口，让我们吃了一惊。

items.example: The apparition vanished at sunrise.
items.exampleCN: 那个幻影在日出时消失了。

items.example: It directs the appearing towards the viewer.
items.exampleCN: 它把「显现」指向观看者。

latinEntries.example: Apparere is the direct source of apparent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: apparere 是 apparent 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 呼吁；恳求；上诉；吸引力；有吸引力
definition_en: an urgent request for help or support; a formal request to a higher court; the quality of being attractive; also to make such a request or to attract
core_image: 把话抛向远处的人，请求他们回应
scene: 洪水过后的村公所里，干部把一张写满名字的纸举起来。The mayor made an appeal to every household for blankets and clean water.
sceneCN: 这里 appeal 是「呼吁；恳求」（第 1 个义项：向众人提出紧急请求）；句意为「镇长向每一户人家呼吁捐出毛毯和干净的水」。画面里有洪水过后的村公所、写满名字的纸和举着纸的干部。

pos.zh: 名词：呼吁；恳求；上诉；吸引力
动词：呼吁；恳求；上诉；有吸引力

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「有吸引力的；动人的」
由本词加 -ant 构成，义为「上诉人」
由否定前缀 un- 加 appealing 构成，义为「没有吸引力的」

senses.title: An urgent request for help
senses.definition: a serious and often public request for help, money, or support
senses.definitionCN: 严肃而常是公开的请求，求取帮助、钱款或支持
senses.example: The mayor made an appeal to every household for blankets and clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 镇长向每一户人家呼吁捐出毛毯和干净的水。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to call out to someone'; the request is a call thrown across distance, hoping for an answer.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「向某人喊话」；这个请求就是一声抛过距离的呼唤，盼着有人回应。

senses.title: A request to a higher court
senses.definition: a formal request asking a higher court to review and change a legal decision
senses.definitionCN: 正式请求更高一级法院复审并改变某项法律裁决
senses.example: The verdict was overturned on appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 那项判决在上诉中被推翻了。
senses.why: In law the call goes upward, to a higher authority; the same 'call out' image is now addressed to the court above.
senses.whyCN: 在法律里，呼唤的方向朝上，向更高的权威发出；同一个「喊话」意象如今对着上级法院。

senses.title: The power to attract
senses.definition: the quality in something that makes people like it or want to be near it
senses.definitionCN: 某事物中使人喜欢它或愿意靠近它的特质
senses.example: The old market has a strong appeal for young visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老市场对年轻游客有很强的吸引力。
senses.why: The call is now silent and internal: the object calls to people without asking them for anything, and they answer by coming.
senses.whyCN: 这里的呼唤是无声而向内的：对象向人发出召唤，却不向人索要什么，而人用前来作为回答。

senses.title: To be attractive to someone
senses.definition: as a verb, to please or interest someone, so that they are drawn towards it
senses.definitionCN: 作动词时，表示使人喜欢或感兴趣，从而被它吸引过去
senses.example: The simple plan appeals to people who dislike waste.
senses.exampleCN: 这个简单的方案打动了不喜欢浪费的人。
senses.why: Here the attraction is felt as an answer: the plan calls, and the people find themselves responding.
senses.whyCN: 这里的吸引力被感受为一种回应：方案发出召唤，人们发现自己响应了。

senses.title: To call upon reason or feelings
senses.definition: in the phrase appeal to, to invoke something such as reason, emotion, or a principle as support
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 appeal to，表示借助理智、情感或某项原则来作为支撑
senses.example: The speaker appealed to the audience's sense of fairness.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲者诉诸听众的公平感。
senses.why: The oldest layer of 'call out' returns: one does not ask for aid but summons a faculty in the listener and asks it to decide.
senses.whyCN: 「喊话」最古老的一层回来了：不是求取援助，而是召唤听者内心的一种能力，请它来作判断。

intro.en: Appeal goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to call out to someone', and every later sense is a variation on that call.
intro.cn: appeal 可上溯到一个表示「向某人喊话」的拉丁动词，此后每个义项都是那声呼唤的变奏。

items.en: Appellare meant 'to address, call upon', built from ad- 'to' and pellere 'drive'; the sense is of driving words towards someone.
items.cn: appellare 表示「向……说话、召唤」，由 ad-「向」与 pellere「驱动」构成；意象是把话推向某人。

items.en: The verb passes into Old French as apeler, 'to call, to summon', and English borrows it.
items.cn: 这个动词进入古法语作 apeler，义为「呼叫、传唤」，英语随后借入。

items.en: English appeal first appears in law, meaning to call a case up to a higher court.
items.cn: 英语 appeal 最早出现在法律语境，意为把案件上诉到更高一级法院。

items.en: The general sense 'urgent request' develops, and the noun can name a plea for help or money.
items.cn: 一般义「紧急请求」发展出来，名词可指为帮助或钱款发出的恳求。

items.en: The sense of attractiveness appears: a thing can appeal to people without asking them for anything.
items.cn: 吸引力义出现：事物可以不向人索求什么，却仍对人发出召唤。

items.en: The word works in law, charity, advertising and argument, always keeping the shape of a call directed at someone.
items.cn: 这个词活跃于法律、慈善、广告与论辩之中，始终保留着「向某人发出呼唤」的形状。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same 'call out' verb; the near-meaning group gathers requests, legal challenges and forms of attraction.
note.cn: 形近组收同出那个「喊话」动词的词；近义组收请求、法律申诉与吸引力方面的词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning attractive or touching.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有吸引力的；动人的」，由本词加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: A noun for the person who brings an appeal in a legal case.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「上诉人」，指在法律案件中提出上诉的一方。

entries.definition: A noun meaning a name or title, from the same 'call' verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「名称、称号」，同出表示「呼叫」的那个动词。

entries.definition: To ask urgently and emotionally for something.
entries.definitionCN: 急切而带感情地请求，语气比 appeal 更卑微。

entries.definition: To ask for something politely, without the urgency of appeal.
entries.definitionCN: 礼貌地提出请求，没有 appeal 那种紧急与公开性。

entries.definition: A formal written request signed by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 由许多人签名的正式书面请求，与 appeal 的公开呼吁义接近。

entries.definition: The quality of drawing people towards something.
entries.definitionCN: 把人吸引到某物那里的特质，对应 appeal 的「吸引力」义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real 'call out' verb and the frames the word takes as noun and verb.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的「喊话」动词，以及这个词作名词与动词时的句式。

normal.en: The core is a call thrown towards someone: ad- 'to' plus pellere 'drive'.
normal.cn: 核心是一声抛向某人的呼唤：ad-「向」加 pellere「驱动」。

normal.en: The legal sense calls upward: a case is appealed to a higher court.
normal.cn: 法律义朝上呼唤：案件被上诉到更高一级法院。

normal.en: The charity sense calls outward: an appeal for blankets and water.
normal.cn: 慈善义朝外呼唤：为毛毯和净水发出呼吁。

normal.en: The attraction sense calls silently: the old market appeals to visitors.
normal.cn: 吸引力义无声地呼唤：老市场吸引着游客。

normal.en: The argument sense summons a faculty: appeal to reason, not to fear.
normal.cn: 论辩义召唤一种能力：诉诸理智，而不是恐惧。

abstract.en: Picture a voice carried across a valley, waiting for someone on the far side to answer.
abstract.cn: 想象一声呼喊越过山谷，等着对面有人回应。

abstract.en: The word is a thread thrown out into the air; the answer may be help, a verdict, or simply a visit.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一根抛向空中的线；回应可能是援助、判决，也可能只是一次到访。

abstract.en: When nobody is asked for anything, the same thread becomes charm: the call that expects no reply.
abstract.cn: 当它不向任何人索求时，同一根线就变成了魅力：一声不期待回应的呼唤。

examples.en: The charity launched an appeal for winter coats.
examples.cn: 那家慈善机构发起了一场募集冬衣的呼吁。

examples.en: The verdict was overturned on appeal.
examples.cn: 那项判决在上诉中被推翻了。

examples.en: The old market has a strong appeal for young visitors.
examples.cn: 这座老市场对年轻游客有很强的吸引力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额皮尔」——镇长举着名单喊「皮尔，你家有毛毯吗」：呼吁

root: appeal 经古法语 apeler 来自拉丁语 appellare「向……说话、召唤」，该动词由 ad-「向」与 pellere「驱动」构成，意象是把话推向某人。十四世纪英语先用于法律，指把案件上诉到更高法院；十六世纪发展出一般义「紧急请求」；十九世纪出现「吸引力」义；现代这个词活跃于法律、慈善、广告与论辩，始终保留「向某人发出呼唤」的形状。

sensesIntro.en: Five uses fan out from one call: an urgent public request, a legal call to a higher court, the silent pull of an attractive thing, the verb of attracting, and the summons of reason or feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个用法从同一声呼唤展开：公开的紧急请求、向更高法院发出的法律呼唤、有魅力之物的无声牵引、表示吸引的动词，以及对理智或情感的召唤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice thrown across a distance, waiting for an answer from the far side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一声越过距离的呼唤，等着对面给出回应。

branches.en: THE HELP LINE: the call asks for blankets, money or support.
branches.cn: 求助线：呼唤求取毛毯、钱款或支持。

branches.en: THE LEGAL LINE: the call goes upward to a higher court.
branches.cn: 法律线：呼唤朝上，传给更高一级法院。

branches.en: THE CHARM LINE: the object calls without asking for anything.
branches.cn: 魅力线：对象发出呼唤，却不索要任何东西。

branches.en: THE PULL LINE: people answer the silent call by coming nearer.
branches.cn: 牵引线：人们用靠近来回应那声无声的呼唤。

branches.en: THE SUMMONS LINE: reason or feeling is called upon to decide.
branches.cn: 召唤线：请理智或情感出面作判断。

intro.en: Appeal is a Latin borrowing whose stem is 'call out'; its English derivatives add ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: appeal 是拉丁语借词，词干意为「喊话」；它的英语派生词只是加上常见后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestry is direct: appellare is the verb behind appeal, and pellere 'drive' sits inside it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语血统是直接的：appellare 是 appeal 背后的动词，而 pellere「驱动」嵌在其中。

items.meaning: to call upon; a call for help
items.example: The appeal reached the whole valley.
items.exampleCN: 那声呼吁传遍了整个山谷。

items.example: The verb drives words towards the listener.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把话推向听者。

items.example: It aims the call at someone.
items.exampleCN: 它把呼唤对准某个人。

items.example: Pellere supplies the push inside the word.
items.exampleCN: pellere 提供了这个词内部的推力。

items.example: The idea sounds appealing at first.
items.exampleCN: 这个想法乍听很吸引人。

items.meaning: a person who appeals a case
items.example: The appellant asked for a new hearing.
items.exampleCN: 上诉人请求重新审理。

items.example: The region has an old appellation.
items.exampleCN: 这个地区有一个古老的名称。

items.example: The grey building looks unappealing.
items.exampleCN: 那栋灰楼看上去毫无吸引力。

items.meaningCN: 由动词构成名词的后缀
items.example: It turns the calling verb into an act.
items.exampleCN: 它把「呼唤」这个动词变成一种行为。

latinEntries.example: Appellare is the direct source of appeal.
latinEntries.exampleCN: appellare 是 appeal 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Pellere sits inside appellare.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pellere 嵌在 appellare 之中。

definition_zh: 出现；显现；显得；似乎；出庭；登台；问世
definition_en: to come into sight; to seem; to be present in public, on stage, or in court; to be published
core_image: 原本看不见的东西，忽然进入视野
scene: 剧场的幕布缓缓拉开，灯光先落在空舞台上。A single figure appeared at the back of the stage, holding an old lantern.
sceneCN: 这里 appeared 是「出现」（第 1 个义项：从看不见变为进入视野）；句意为「一个身影出现在舞台后方，手里提着一盏旧灯」。画面里有缓缓拉开的幕布、空舞台和提着旧灯的身影。

pos.zh: 动词：出现；显现；显得；似乎；出庭；登台

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「出现；外表」
与本词同出拉丁语 apparere，义为「明显的；表面上的」
由 apparent 加 -ly 构成，义为「看来；据说」
由同一拉丁词根派生，义为「幽灵；幻影」

senses.title: To come into sight
senses.definition: to become visible, especially suddenly or unexpectedly
senses.definitionCN: 变得可见，尤指突然或出乎意料地进入视野
senses.example: A single figure appeared at the back of the stage, holding an old lantern.
senses.exampleCN: 一个身影出现在舞台后方，手里提着一盏旧灯。
senses.why: The Latin verb means 'come into view'; the thing was not seen, and then it was, so the change is the whole event.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「进入视野」；那东西原先看不见，随后被看见，这个变化本身就是整件事。

senses.title: To seem or look a certain way
senses.definition: to give the impression of being something, especially when followed by an adjective or to be
senses.definitionCN: 给人某种印象，尤指后接形容词或 to be 结构
senses.example: The plan appears to be working.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案看来正在奏效。
senses.why: What shows itself to the eye is taken as what is true, so 'comes into view' easily slides into 'seems to be'.
senses.whyCN: 显现在眼前的东西被当作真实，于是「进入视野」很容易滑向「看来是」。

senses.title: To be present in public
senses.definition: to be present at a public event or before a court, often as a required act
senses.definitionCN: 出现在公开场合或法庭上，常指必须履行的到场
senses.example: She appeared in court on Monday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她周一上午出庭了。
senses.why: A person who must be seen shows himself in the place where witnesses and officials expect him.
senses.whyCN: 一个必须被看见的人，就在证人与官员等候他的地方把自己显出来。

senses.title: To perform or be published
senses.definition: to take part in a performance, or to be published or released to the public
senses.definitionCN: 参与演出，或被出版、发行到公众面前
senses.example: Her first novel appeared in the spring of that year.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部小说在那年春天问世。
senses.why: A book or a performer enters the public eye exactly as a figure enters a stage: before that, it existed unseen.
senses.whyCN: 一本书或一位表演者进入公众视野，正像一个身影走上舞台：在此之前，它存在却不被看见。

senses.title: To be found or noticed
senses.definition: to be found in a place or among a group, especially after a search
senses.definitionCN: 在某处或某群之中被发现，尤指经过搜寻之后
senses.example: The missing keys appeared under a pile of old newspapers.
senses.exampleCN: 丢失的钥匙出现在一叠旧报纸下面。
senses.why: Searching presupposes absence; when the object finally shows itself, the word marks the end of the search.

intro.en: Appear comes from a Latin verb meaning 'come into sight', and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: appear 来自一个表示「进入视野」的拉丁动词，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: Apparere 'come into view, show oneself' was built from ad- 'to' and parere 'come forth, be visible'.
items.cn: apparere「进入视野、显现自身」由 ad-「向」与 parere「出现、可见」构成。

items.en: The verb passes into Old French as aparoir 'to appear, to show oneself'.
items.cn: 这个动词进入古法语作 aparoir，义为「出现、显露自身」。

items.en: English borrows the verb, first in the plain sense 'come into sight'.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词，最初取「进入视野」的朴素义项。

items.en: The sense 'seem, look' develops, especially in the frame appear to be.
items.cn: 「显得、看来」义发展出来，尤其在 appear to be 这一句式中。

items.en: The word extends to books, plays and public life: a work or a person can appear before an audience.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到书籍、戏剧与公共生活：一部作品或一个人可以出现在观众面前。

items.en: The verb covers sight, impression, performance and publication, while its relatives keep the same 'visible' core.
items.cn: 这个动词覆盖视觉、印象、演出与出版，而它的同族词保留着同一个「可见」核心。

abstract.en: Its double life: entering the eye and entering the mind are the same motion.

scene: 剧院后台的门被推开，化妆师最后看了一眼镜中的演员。Her appearance on stage was greeted with a long round of applause.

senses.title: The act of appearing
senses.definition: the act of coming into sight or being present before people
senses.definitionCN: 进入视野或出现在人们面前这一行为
senses.example: Her appearance on stage was greeted with a long round of applause.
senses.exampleCN: 她在台上的登场赢得了一长阵掌声。
senses.why: The noun names the event of the Latin verb: a figure that was behind the curtain now stands where everyone can see it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名那个拉丁动词的事件：原本在幕后的身影，如今站在人人看得见的地方。

senses.title: The outward look
senses.definition: the way a person or thing looks to others, especially on the outside
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或一件东西呈现给别人的样子，尤指外在的样子
senses.example: The building has changed little in appearance.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼在外观上几乎没有变化。
senses.why: What appears is also what is judged, so the event of appearing turns into the permanent surface by which things are recognized.
senses.whyCN: 显现出来的东西也正是被评判的东西，于是「出现」这一事件转成事物借以被认出的持久表面。

senses.title: A public or formal presence
senses.definition: a single act of attending or being seen in public, often noted by others
senses.definitionCN: 一次出席或在公众面前被看见的行为，常被别人注意到
senses.example: He made a brief appearance at the reception.
senses.exampleCN: 他在招待会上短暂露了一面。
senses.why: Public life counts appearances: being seen once at the right place can carry as much weight as a whole speech.
senses.whyCN: 公共生活要算计「露面」：在合适的场合被看见一次，分量可能抵得上一整篇讲话。

senses.title: A performance or published work
senses.definition: an occasion of performing, or the publication and arrival of a work before the public
senses.definitionCN: 一次演出的场合，或一部作品出版并来到公众面前的时刻
senses.example: The appearance of her first novel surprised the critics.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一部小说的问世让评论家们吃了一惊。
senses.why: A book appears in the world as an actor appears on stage: both cross from obscurity into the public eye.
senses.whyCN: 一本书在世界中「出现」，正如演员在舞台上「出现」：两者都是从默默无闻跨入公众视野。

senses.title: Outward impression, as opposed to fact
senses.definition: in phrases such as to all appearances, the impression given, which may differ from the truth
senses.definitionCN: 用于 to all appearances 一类短语，指给出的印象，可能与事实不符
senses.example: To all appearances, the two firms were still friendly rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 从表面上看，这两家公司仍是友好的竞争对手。
senses.why: Since appearance is only the surface, the noun can also warn that the surface is not the whole story.
senses.whyCN: 既然 appearance 只是表面，这个名词也能提醒：表面并不等于全部实情。

intro.en: Appearance is the noun built on appear, and it inherits the Latin idea of 'coming into view'.
intro.cn: appearance 是建立在 appear 之上的名词，继承了拉丁语「进入视野」的观念。

items.en: Apparere 'come into view' is the verb behind the whole family, built from ad- 'to' and parere 'come forth'.

items.en: French forms the noun aparance from the verb, and English takes the pattern with its own suffix -ance.

items.en: English appearance is first recorded in the sense 'the act of appearing', close to the verb.
items.cn: 英语 appearance 最初有记载的义项是「出现这一行为」，与动词义贴近。

items.en: The sense 'outward look' becomes common, and the word starts to judge as well as to describe.
items.cn: 「外表、外观」义变得常见，这个词开始既描述也评判。

items.en: The noun covers stage, court, publication and surface impression; the phrase to all appearances marks the doubt.
items.cn: 这个名词覆盖舞台、法庭、出版与表面印象；短语 to all appearances 则标出那份怀疑。
